title: ENTRY — multiple entry points into a single subroutine, sharing local state
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE STATS_INIT(N)
C     Single program unit with three entry points: STATS_INIT,
C     STATS_ADD, STATS_GET. All three share the SAVEd locals SUM
C     and COUNT -- this is a stateful API built into one routine.
C     Each ENTRY is callable by name; the body that runs is
C     determined by which ENTRY was called. F90 deprecated this;
C     F2008 marked it obsolescent.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N
      REAL    X
      REAL    SUM
      INTEGER COUNT
      SAVE    SUM, COUNT
      SUM   = 0.0
      COUNT = 0
      RETURN
      ENTRY STATS_ADD(X)
      SUM   = SUM + X
      COUNT = COUNT + 1
      RETURN
      ENTRY STATS_GET(X)
      X = SUM / REAL(COUNT)
      RETURN
      END
notes: ENTRY is the closest F77 came to an object: three callable methods sharing state via SAVE. The natural Java/C# rewrite is a class. The spec must capture: (a) each ENTRY's individual contract, (b) the shared state semantic, (c) the re-entrancy / thread-safety question — the SAVE makes this single-instance by design.
